findings.title: Auto Backup enabled; expense database, receipt photos and CSV backup are not excluded
findings.explanation: allowBackup is true. The rules only exclude three SharedPreferences files. receipts.db (merchants, amounts, city, encrypted notes), the receipt photos in filesDir/receipts, and the plaintext CSV in filesDir/backup are all uploaded to Google cloud backup and device transfer. The notes are encrypted with a Keystore key that will not restore on a new device, so those notes become unreadable. Exclude the database, the files/receipts and files/backup directories, or set allowBackup=false.

findings.title: Exported deep-link WebView activity: host check can be bypassed and the page gets a JS bridge
findings.explanation: HelpActivity is exported and BROWSABLE. Any web page or app can set the page URL through the pennyjar://help?page= link or the intent extra. isHelpPage relies on android.net.Uri.parse for the host. Android's Uri parser and WebView's URL parser handle some malformed URLs differently (for example backslash or userinfo tricks). A crafted URL could pass the check while WebView loads another site with JavaScript enabled and the PennyJar bridge attached. The bridge currently exposes only appVersion() and close(), so the impact is small, but any future bridge method would be exposed. Parse the URL strictly, for example by comparing against a fixed prefix or using java.net.URI, and consider dropping the bridge or the exported deep link.

findings.title: Play Data safety and privacy disclosures need review (location, financial data, analytics, account deletion)
findings.explanation: The app collects coarse location (city) and expense data and sends them to your server. It sends a user ID and usage events to Mixpanel when the user opts in. It uses Mixpanel with automatic events, and it offers in-app account deletion. The Play Data safety form must declare all of this, including sharing with Mixpanel. Because the app lets users create accounts, Play also requires a web-based account deletion URL in the console. The privacy policy at pennyjar.example/privacy must match what the app does. The Consent screen text describes only screens and features, so check that it also covers the user ID and amount-band and category events. Confirm all of this before release.
